source.author: stat
source.text: vix credo et nuntius: omnes procubuere, omnes, noctis vaga lumina testor et socium manes et te, mala protinus ales, qua redeo, non hanc lacrimis meruisse nec astu crudelem veniam atque inhonorae munera lucis, sed mihi iussa deum placitoque ignara moveri Atropos atque olim non haec data ianua leti eripuere necem, iamque ut mihi prodiga vitae pectora et extremam nihil horrescentia mortem aspicias: bellum infandum ominibusque negatam movisti, funeste, aciem; dum pellere leges, et consanguineo gestis regnare superbus exsule, te series orbarum excisa domorum planctibus assiduis, te diro horrore volantes quinquaginta animae circum noctesque diesque assilient; neque enim ipse moror.
source.text_original: vix credo et nuntius: omnes / procubuere, omnes, noctis vaga lumina testor / et socium manes et te, mala protinus ales, / qua redeo, non hanc lacrimis meruisse nec astu / crudelem veniam atque inhonorae munera lucis, / sed mihi iussa deum placitoque ignara moveri / Atropos atque olim non haec data ianua leti / eripuere necem, iamque ut mihi prodiga vitae / pectora et extremam nihil horrescentia mortem / aspicias: bellum infandum ominibusque negatam / movisti, funeste, aciem; dum pellere leges, / et consanguineo gestis regnare superbus / exsule, te series orbarum excisa domorum / planctibus assiduis, te diro horrore volantes / quinquaginta animae circum noctesque diesque / assilient; neque enim ipse moror.
source.text_english: I can scarcely believe it, and the messenger as well: they have all fallen, all of them—I call to witness the wandering lights of night and the shades of my comrade and you, evil bird, straightway where I return—not by tears has she earned this, nor by guile, that cruel pardon and the gifts of a dishonored life, but because, by the gods’ command and without her knowledge, Atropos was moved by their will, and long ago the door of death not granted her, snatched away the killing; and now, as though you would behold for me breasts prodigal of life and fearing nothing but the last death: you have stirred up, accursed one, the unspeakable war and the battle-line denied by the omens; while you strive to drive out the laws and, proud as an exile, to rule over your kin, the sequence of bereaved houses, cut down, shall with unceasing lamentation, with dreadful horror, and fifty souls in flight, assail you night and day; for I myself am not delayed.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: hinc quoque missus adest quamvis arcentibus Idmon alitibus; sed turpe viro timuisse futura.
reuse.text_original: hinc quoque missus adest quamvis arcentibus Idmon / alitibus; sed turpe viro timuisse futura.
reuse.text_english: From here too Idmon is sent, though the birds were keeping him back; but it is shameful for a man to have feared what was to come.
